title: Palace to Cayetano: Lead the way

blocks.text: Senate Minority Leader Alan Cayetano on February 9, 2026.

This was Malacañang’s challenge to Senate Minority Leader Alan Cayetano, who urged the central bank and economic managers on Monday to come up with a way for generous Filipinos to voluntarily share in repaying the country’s debt.

“He (Cayetano) said it’s voluntary. So it is hard to craft a law if it becomes mandatory. But if there are kind-hearted persons who are willing to start it, it would be better if we see Sen. Alan Cayetano himself starting it,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said yesterday.
According to Castro, Cayetano could “serve as a model” by contributing money to reduce the Philippines’ debt.
Cayetano floated the idea during the Senate’s plenary debates on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for next year.
He noted that every Filipino owes more than P170,000 since the national government debt stood at P19.66 trillion as of the third quarter.
Despite the backlash, Cayetano stood firm on his proposal.
He pointed out that the lack of such a mechanism for volunteerism reflects a deeper “crisis of confidence” and distrust in public officials.

“There’s no mechanism because no one thinks that anyone will donate because we think our government, not just this government, but government after government, it’s just kung sino mas kurap,” he said. — Neil Jayson Servallos
